key_insight: LLM tool-use agents that perform well on static benchmarks can still degrade sharply when queries, tools, and interactions shift in open-world settings.
engineering_relevance: For production agent systems, robustness to changing tools and user behavior is as important as raw benchmark accuracy, especially in dynamic software pipelines and knowledge workflows.
method: Defined OpenAgent, an open-world tool-use setting with shifts across query, action, observation, and domain dimensions.
Built a controlled sandbox with a four-tier shift hierarchy: Perception, Interaction, Reasoning, and Internalization.
Proposed Perturbation-Augmented Fine-Tuning to improve SFT robustness via disturbance-based training.
evidence_signal: The authors ran a comprehensive set of controlled experiments in the sandbox and found that both SFT-trained and RL-trained agents suffer performance degradation under open environmental shifts.
watch_item: Robustness gains from perturbation-augmented fine-tuning may depend on how well the sandbox perturbations match real deployment shifts, so transfer to live systems should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Can Agents Generalize to the Open World? Unveiling the Fragility of Static Training in Tool Use
